claim: For fixed \(p_0>0\) and \(q>0\), every integer \(n\ge\max\{2,p_0\}\), and model parameters \(b,c_0>0\), let \(B\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}\) have \(B_{ii}=1\) and independent \(B_{ij}\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_0/n)\) for \(i\ne j\). Define \(S_{ij}=\sum_{k\ne i}B_{ki}B_{kj}\), \(K_R=\exp\!\big(p_0[\exp(2+p_0(e-1))-1]\big)\), \(K_C=\exp\!\big(p_0(e-1)+p_0[\exp(1+p_0(e-1))-1]\big)\), and \(u_n=(q+1)\log n+\log(K_R+K_C)\). In the homogeneous quadratic-benefit, quadratic-cost networked public-goods model of Cheng, Deng, and Ma, if \(c_0/(2b)>u_n\), then the Nash equilibrium is unique with probability at least \(1-n^{-q}\).

correctness.rationale: For each fixed row, the exact exponential moment is \(\mathbb{E}e^{R_i}=[1-p+pe^2(1-p+pe)^{n-2}]^{n-1}\); for each fixed column it is \(\mathbb{E}e^{C_j}=(1-p+pe)^{n-1}[1-p+pe(1-p+pe)^{n-2}]^{n-1}\). Using \((1-p+pe)^{n-2}\le\exp(p_0(e-1))\) and \(1+x\le\exp(x)\) bounds these by \(K_R\) and \(K_C\). Markov's inequality and a union bound give probability at most \(n^{-q}\) that any row or column sum exceeds \(u_n\). The induced-norm inequality \(\|S\|_2\le\sqrt{\|S\|_1\|S\|_\infty}\) then yields \(\|S\|_2\le u_n\), and the cited uniqueness criterion applies when \(c_0/(2b)>u_n\). The proof does not rely on independence among row or column sums.

originality.rationale: The primary paper states an \(O(\sqrt{n})\) random-network threshold and explicitly leaves polylogarithmic dependence for further study. The present claim independently establishes a concrete \(O(\log n)\) sufficient threshold with probability at least \(1-n^{-q}\) for the same sparse directed Bernoulli model. The proof controls both row and column sums, so it does not rely on a one-sided row-sum bound for the nonsymmetric operator norm. The inspected general uniqueness and random-matrix results use different assumptions or matrices. This is an application-level sharpening, not a new general concentration theorem.

value.rationale: The source paper explicitly leaves a polylogarithmic random-network uniqueness bound as a future direction. The logarithmic sufficient threshold improves the asymptotic curvature scaling from \(\sqrt{n}\) to \(\log n\) and upgrades the probability statement from at least \(1/2\) to at least \(1-n^{-q}\). This is a concrete, mathematically motivated improvement for a model of networked digital public-goods provision, while the result clearly states that its constants are conservative and the threshold is not sharp.
